speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing sudden vertigo; to help narrow this down, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea along with the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the brief duration of only three minutes is very telling. Did you experience any temporary hearing loss, muffled hearing, or tinnitus right when the spinning started? Also, did you have any headache, double vision, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The brief 3-minute duration of spontaneous vertigo without auditory symptoms or neurological deficits is classic for BPPV, likely involving posterior canal debris.
